Ruling: batch #144 item 5 · letter A (for blocks whose published `data` row is the object arm, `SchemaRenderer` stops spreading `data` as a prop) with a stop-gate · maintainer 「9593 A,其他同意」 2026-09-17T11:32Z

Director seat, summon #24, `session_01Wj1HUjzyeiBQ8atRf1ZhaL`. Presented with the recommendation **A** plus a stop-gate; the maintainer's reply covers this item under 「其他同意」. Facts (triage's live re-read on `origin/main`): `ObjectGrid.tsx:1161` `data: passedData` lifted with an unconditional `Array.isArray`, `:1315` documents it as the host path (ListView hands down rows it already fetched); objectui#8348 judged `schema.data` only; gating the props channel on the same arm was declined there because it would delete the host path.

## Ruling — **A**, with a stop-gate the dev runs before writing anything

- **Measure first**: enumerate how every host delivers `data` to `object-grid` / `object-map` (direct React prop vs. injection into a schema node that `SchemaRenderer` then spreads). Cite counts with the control that fires.
  - All hosts use the direct prop ⇒ **A lands**: for blocks whose published `data` row is the `ViewData` object arm, `SchemaRenderer` no longer spreads an authored `data` as a prop; the authored key is judged once, by the #8348 ladder; the host path is untouched. Pin: an authored bare array on `object-grid` / `object-map` no longer draws through `SchemaRenderer`; ListView's rows still render.
  - Any host injects `data` through the schema node ⇒ **stop and report**: A would delete a working path; the direction becomes **B** (a dedicated host prop name), which is a published-surface addition and returns to the maintainer as its own line.
- Read `ObjectCalendar.recordSourceMembers-8314.test.tsx`'s warning first: the obvious pin here passes without measuring anything.
- `Clause-②`: no for A as ruled (narrowing a runtime behaviour back to a published row, `SchemaRenderer` internals) — the claiming seat re-declares if the diff touches a published `@object-ui/*` prop surface.

Four-facet reading: ① one name one meaning on these blocks; ② both legs serve real scenarios, so the host leg must be proven safe before the authored leg is closed; ③ the authored-but-refused spelling stops drawing, so the AI stops learning it; ④ A adds no surface.

## Execution

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`, `domain:ui`, p2 stands. objectui#8348 itself is ⛔ not reopened; objectui#7210 half 2 and objectui#4631 stay their own cards.

Maintainer ruling of 2026-09-17T11:32Z, batch #144 item 5, **letter A with a stop-gate**, 「其他同意」. ⛔ objectui#8348 is not reopened; objectui#7210 half 2 and objectui#4631 stay their own cards.

## Re-verified on `f73521f93` — every leg is mine, ⛔ not relayed

| probe | reading |
|---|---|
| the props carrier | `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx:1161` — `data: passedData,` |

| **firing control**, same instrument | `Array.isArray` → **16** hits in that file ⇒ file and predicate are live, so a zero elsewhere would have meant something |
| `SchemaRenderer` | `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` |

## ⭐ The stop-gate runs BEFORE anything is written, and it can end this dispatch

> **Measure first**: enumerate how every host delivers `data` to `object-grid` / `object-map` — a direct React prop, versus injection into a schema node that `SchemaRenderer` then spreads. **Cite counts with the control that fires.**

- **All hosts use the direct prop ⇒ A lands.** For blocks whose published `data` row is the `ViewData` object arm, `SchemaRenderer` stops spreading an authored `data` as a prop; the authored key is judged **once**, by the objectui#8348 ladder; the host path is untouched.
  **Pin**: an authored bare array on `object-grid` / `object-map` no longer draws through `SchemaRenderer`, **and ListView's rows still render**. Both halves, or the pin measures half the ruling.
- **Any host injects `data` through the schema node ⇒ ⛔ STOP AND REPORT.** A would delete a working path, and the direction becomes **B** (a dedicated host prop name) — a published-surface addition that returns to the maintainer as its own line. ⛔ Do not take B here, and ⛔ do not "just handle both".

⚠️ A stop is the **designed outcome** of that branch, not a failure. Report the enumeration with its control and stop.

## ⚠️⚠️ The ruling itself warns the obvious pin is vacuous — read that warning first

> *"Read `ObjectCalendar.recordSourceMembers-8314.test.tsx`'s warning first: the obvious pin here passes without measuring anything."*

The file is at `packages/plugin-calendar/src/__tests__/ObjectCalendar.recordSourceMembers-8314.test.tsx` — I confirmed it exists and ⛔ did **not** quote a line from it, because I did not locate the warning text itself; read it yourself. ⭐ This is the same class this lane has paid for twice in two days: a pin whose assertion cannot fail, and an equality where two absences compare equal. Build the pin so it **fails** on the pre-fix tree, and show it failing.

## ⛔ Hard constraints

- ⛔ **Do not gate the host path.** objectui#8348 declined exactly that trade, and the ruling keeps it declined: at the component boundary the authored key and the host key are indistinguishable, so closing the authoring gap by the same arm deletes a working path.
- ⛔ **Only blocks whose published `data` row is the `ViewData` object arm** are in scope. A block whose row is `z.array(...)` is objectui#8348's business and is already judged.
- ⛔ **Do not reopen objectui#8348**, and ⛔ do not fold in objectui#7210 half 2 or objectui#4631.
- **Clause-②: `no`** as ruled — a runtime narrowing back to a published row, in `SchemaRenderer` internals. ⚠️ **Re-declare at delivery.** ⭐ A warning from this seat's own measurement an hour ago: *"not named in the package entry" is not the same as "not on the published face"* — a type or prop referenced by any **exported signature** is emitted into the published `.d.ts` even when the entry never names it. If your diff touches anything reachable that way, clause ② flips ⇒ **stop and report**. Mechanical floor `^\+export` = **0**.
- ⛔ objectui `AGENTS.md:316`: never `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease`, never push to `main`. Absolute, not tiered by seat, and no instruction of mine overrides it.
- ⚠️ Scope-pinned card ⇒ AGENTS.md #11's opportunistic citation repair does ⛔ **not** apply.

## Return

The host enumeration **with its firing control** (that is the stop-gate and it is a deliverable either way), which branch it put you on, the pin failing on the pre-fix tree, the `clause_2` field re-measured, and any premise of mine you falsified. ⚠️ **Ten of my premises have been falsified by lanes over the last two shifts**, most of them assertions about something I had not just read, or had read without asking *which object is this*. Treat every address and count above as mine to be checked. A clean stop — especially at the stop-gate — is a **full success**.

## ⛔ Nothing to implement — ruling A **was already landed before this card was graded**. Closing as satisfied.

### ⭐ The same open question was carded twice and ruled twice

objectui#9571 and this card are both objectui#8348's **open question 2**. The director seat filed one and ruled it **Q2-C** in decision batch #136; this one was ruled **A** in batch #144 item 5 on 2026-09-17T11:32Z — **a day after the fix for it had already merged**. The two letters name the same shape, and the landed code is verbatim that shape.

⇒ The ruling is satisfied, not stale: what it asks for is in the tree.

### The stop-gate was run anyway, and it answers branch A with a control that fires

⭐ The lane did not take "already done" as licence to skip the measurement, and the enumeration stands on its own:

- **Leg B — a host injecting `data` through the schema node for `object-grid` / `object-map`: ZERO.**
- **FIRING CONTROL**: the same grep shape finds a real injection at `ListView.tsx:2976` — `...(schema.data ? { data: schema.data } : {})` — on the **object-gantt** branch of the **same switch in the same file**. ⇒ the instrument can see leg B where leg B exists, so the zero is a reading of the tree and not a blind spot.
- **Leg A — all hosts.** `ListView.tsx:4457` and `ObjectView.tsx:2217` both render `SchemaRenderer` with a sibling `data` React prop; the node builders are closed picklists that cannot emit `data` (`FLAT_MAP_CONFIG_KEYS` is a 7-key allowlist, so adding it would be a type error).

And the pins were proved **non-vacuous by ablation of the landed fix** — rewriting the arm test to an unreachable value restores the pre-fix tree and turns **14 of 55** red, while every must-not-change host row stays green. That asymmetry is what makes the second half of the ruled pin a real assertion rather than a restatement of the first.

### ⛔ My eleventh falsified premise, and it is a NEW class

The other ten were *"an assertion about something I had not just read, or had read without asking which object is this."* This one is different: **I never asked whether the ruled work was already done.**

I read the card body, both comments and the full ruling — and the card's own Dedup section says, verbatim: *"No duplicate sweep with a lit control was run for this card — REST `/search/*` answers 403 for this session by design … **the taker should check**."* **I was the taker. I did not check.**

⇒ New standing item for this seat, before any dispatch of a ruled card: **is the ruling already satisfied in the tree?** A ruling is a description of a desired state, and a desired state can arrive by another route.

### Filed separately

**objectui#9758** — the objectui#9571 strip is applied to `componentProps`, but the legacy `props` alias bag is spread **after** it, so an authored `props: { data: [ … ] }` still takes the prop seat the ruling removed. Measured at the props bag only, ⛔ not end-to-end, and fenced from this card by objectui#7210 half 2 and objectui#4795 pending question 2.

⇒ Closing as **completed** — satisfied by objectui#9571 / PR objectui#9578 — with the `pm:*` state stripped in the same write. ⛔ objectui#8348 is not reopened.
